text:
rachel_cs: Putting up a short 'offline-friendly' onboarding cheat for customers with intermittent connectivity and tight token budgets. Want something we can drop in email + attach to the low-touch onboarding.

rachel_cs: Key goals: keep UX snappy on flaky networks, avoid surprise bills, and surface renewal risk early so CS can do proactive outreach.

rachel_cs: Quick checklist (1 page):
- server-side prefill: push 2 starter messages when a session starts to reduce client cold tokens.
- offline queue: client should buffer up to 5 user inputs and flush as a small batch when connectivity returns.
- prefer concatenation for single coherent reply; prefer small batches (2-3) for parallel independent results.
- streaming only for typing/real-time UX; disable streaming on cellular when packet loss > 10%.
- cache prefixes for 15-45s depending on session churn.
- set "burst_mode" flag for short-term capacity increases and a 48h auto-expire.

tom_se: love the offline queue idea. add a simple debounce so clients don't flood when reconnecting. also include a copy-paste curl + node snippet.

rachel_cs: adding snippets now, they'll be tiny.

rachel_cs: ```
# lightweight batch flush (curl) - good for queued mobile sends
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","inputs":["queued1","queued2"],"max_tokens":100,"stream":false}'

# node pseudo - debounce + flush after reconnect
let queue = []
function enqueue(msg){ queue.push(msg); if(queue.length>5) queue.shift(); }
async function flush(){ if(queue.length===0) return; await client.generate({model:'redwood-mini', inputs:queue.splice(0,3), max_tokens:120}); }
// on reconnect: setTimeout(flush, 250)  // short debounce
```

nina_sre: ops additions to include:
- cache prefix TTL = 30s for most mobile sessions; increase to 60s for low-churn enterprise sessions.
- per-tenant concurrency default = 3, with a limit toggle CS can request.
- renewals: flag "renewal_early_warning" when 3-day rolling avg token consumption > 60% AND error-rate (5xx or timeouts) > 3% for same window.
- when renewal_early_warning is set, auto-create a CS task with last 7 days token graph + suggested mitigations (concat prompts, reduce max_tokens, enable burst_mode).

ben_sales: suggest we include a short outreach script for those flagged, and a checklist of mitigations CS can offer (1: prompt audit, 2: temporary burst, 3: tailored quota).

rachel_cs: draft outreach copy: "Hi <name> — we see some connectivity variance and rising token use in your app. We can help reduce token spend and enable a short burst while you stabilize. Quick 20-min call or a few prompt tweaks — what works?"

ben_sales: short and sweet, good. Also add a line for enterprise customers: offer a free 1-week burst trial to avoid churn.

nina_sre: small SRE UX tip to include: when streaming on flaky networks, send an initial 64-char prefix via a small sync call to get first bytes, then open stream for remainder. reduces tail latency.

rachel_cs: adding that. Also a recommended health rule: if client reports >2 reconnects per session for 24h plus token-spike >30% day-on-day, mark customer as "engagement-risk" and escalate to CSM for a check-in.

infra_bot: created Confluence doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/offline-friendly-onboard (permissions: customer-success, product)

tom_se: one more nit: include header example X-Client-Network: offline|cellular|wifi so SRE routing rules can route lightweight requests differently.

rachel_cs: good call, added example header and I'll tag the network routing runbook. If no objections I'll publish this as 'offline-friendly onboarding cheat' and attach to mobile kickoff template by EOD. Please comment with edits here.
